display.title: Episode 341: The Storyteller, Chapter 4 (Elul)
display.summary_short: 341 weeks on the air and the children's parade to greet Moshiach, the Hakochainik march, Shema with a first-grade class, and Rabbi Yehuda forgets every story at the rich man's table.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week after Rosh Chodesh Elul 5748. Marking 341 weeks on the air, Uncle Yossi promises the show will continue even after Moshiach comes, broadcasting from Yerushalayim, and describes the great parade out of golus led by Jewish children, just as the children were first to recognize Hashem at the Exodus. After the Hakochainik march, the story resumes: Rabbi Yehuda reaches the rich merchant's guarded mansion, where the guards eagerly usher him in. A first-grade class from a Boro Park girls' school recites the Shema. Reb Yitzchak offers a thousand gold pieces for every Baal Shem Tov story he has not heard, locks the door and lights a candle, but Rabbi Yehuda finds he cannot remember a single story and breaks down in tears; the merchant calmly gives him a meal and a room, leaving Rabbi Yehuda puzzled. Uncle Yossi then recalls the first shofar of Elul, invites letters about it, and explains that the shofar is an alarm to prepare for the Yomim Nora'im. Candle-lighting time, a 'ksivah vachasimah tovah' wish and the Dial-a-Jewish-Story line close the show.
display.lesson: Keep hoping for Moshiach every day, and use the shofar of Elul as a wake-up call to come close to Hashem.
